Northwind Logistics — Quarterly Operations Review

Prepared for the board of directors, this review covers the third quarter of the fiscal year. Volumes rose across the northern corridor while the coastal depots absorbed the usual seasonal peak. Customer satisfaction held steady at ninety-two percent, and on-time delivery improved by four points.

Three themes shaped the quarter: tighter fuel contracts, a smaller fleet of leased vans, and the gradual replacement of paper manifests with handheld scanning. Each change reduced cost per parcel without adding headcount. The board asked for a deeper look at depot staffing before the next planning cycle.

Capital Projects Update

The photovoltaic pilot in Rotterdam finished commissioning ahead of schedule. Panels now cover two warehouse roofs and supply roughly a third of daytime demand. The finance team expects a payback period under six years at current tariffs.

A second project, the automated sorting line in Leeds, remains in acceptance testing. Throughput meets the design target, but the reject rate is still above the agreed threshold. The vendor will run a further two weeks of trials before handover. Meanwhile, the depot expansion in Valencia cleared its environmental review and can proceed to tender.

Risk register changes: fuel hedging moved to a rolling twelve-month ladder; the older forklift fleet is now scheduled for replacement in the spring; and insurance premiums rose modestly after the storm damage in August.

People and Operations

Headcount closed at four hundred and six, slightly below plan because two engineering roles remain open. Voluntary turnover fell for the third consecutive quarter. The apprenticeship programme welcomed twelve new starters, and the internal driver academy graduated its first cohort.

Safety performance improved: recordable incidents dropped to three, all minor, and near-miss reporting doubled after the new mobile form went live. The operations team credits the increase to easier reporting rather than a rise in hazardous conditions.

Looking ahead, the board approved a modest capital envelope for the next two quarters. Priorities are completing the Leeds handover, opening the Valencia tender, and standardising depot dashboards so site managers compare like with like.
